# PRD 003: seat messaging permissions

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 003-seat-permissions.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

<a id="meta"></a>

## Meta

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| title | PRD 003: seat messaging permissions |
| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-04 |
| owner | pij-far-jackal |
| summary | Seats can message any seat by default, but a seat can be locked down to a small set, such as its parent and the prime. Parent and prime are always reachable. A sender is told when the recipient can't reply to it. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

A capability for keeping seats from influencing each other. Some seats should not be talked into things by other seats: a reviewer that must stay independent, a seat working for one customer that should not hear from another customer's seats, or a specialist that should stay out of side conversations. There is no specific case yet, but customer deployments will need it. Today any seat can message any other. Locking a seat down must never strand it, so it can always reach its parent and the prime; and anyone who messages a locked seat must know straight away that it cannot answer them directly, so they don't wait for a reply that cannot come.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-prime | prime | To lock down seats that should stay in their lane. |
| a-parent | parent seat | To be the one route a locked child always has. |
| a-locked | locked seat | To know who it may message and how to route anything else. |
| a-sender | sender | To know at send time when a reply cannot come back to it. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | Open by default; restriction is opt-in per seat or per role. |
| g-2 | A locked seat is never stranded: parent and prime are always reachable. |
| g-3 | Nobody waits for a reply that the policy forbids. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | Authentication between machines or between daemons. |
| n-2 | Controlling what a seat may read on disk or in the store. |
| n-3 | Replacing the existing hold on unverified cross-session senders. |

| req-01 | Open by default | With no policy set, a seat may message any seat, as today. Nothing has to be configured for a fleet that doesn't want restrictions. | any seat | must | [ ] planned | `pij send` between two seats with no policy behaves exactly as before; no new refusal appears. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-02 | A seat can be locked down | A seat's send policy is one of: `open` (default), `parent-and-prime`, or an allow list of seat ids and `role:&lt;id&gt;` addresses. It is set at spawn (`pij spawn … --can-message &lt;policy&gt;`) or later (`pij permissions set &lt;seat&gt; &lt;policy&gt; --reason`). | prime | must | [ ] planned | A seat spawned with `--can-message parent-and-prime` is refused when it messages a sibling, and delivers to its parent and the prime. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-03 | Parent and prime are always reachable | Whatever the policy says, a seat can always message its immediate parent and its community's prime. A policy cannot remove them, and an allow list that omits them still includes them. | any seat | must | [ ] planned | An allow list of one unrelated seat still delivers to the parent and the prime; setting a policy that tries to exclude them is accepted with the floor shown. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-04 | Enforced by the daemon, with an actionable refusal | The daemon checks the policy on every send path: direct sends, FYIs, `role:` sends and output notifications. A refused send names the policy, who set it, and who the seat may message, for example `E-RS-SEND-NOT-PERMITTED: pij-x may message only its parent pij-y and the prime pij-z (policy parent-and-prime, set by pij-y: reason)`. | any seat | must | [ ] planned | One test per send path shows the refusal with the allowed recipients; nothing is queued for a refused send. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-05 | A sender is told when the recipient can't reply | When seat A messages seat B and B's policy does not allow B to message A, the message is still delivered, and A is told in the send receipt that B cannot reply to it directly and that replies come back through B's parent. B's copy says the same, so B routes its answer through its parent instead of failing. | requester | must | [ ] planned | A sibling messaging a locked seat gets a receipt saying it cannot reply; the locked seat's message carries the same note; its attempt to reply directly is refused with the route to use. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-06 | Replies and outputs follow the same rule | An output notification to a requester the seat may not message goes to the seat's parent instead, and the requester learns at send time that this will happen. The output record itself stays readable by anyone with `pij outputs`. | requester | must | [ ] planned | A locked seat answering a sibling's request notifies its parent, and the sibling's receipt said so at send time. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-07 | Roles carry a default policy | A role definition can set a default send policy that seats assigned to it inherit; a seat-level policy overrides it. The directory view shows each role's and seat's policy. | prime | should | [ ] planned | A seat assigned to a role with `parent-and-prime` gets that policy; a seat override wins; `pij directory` shows both. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-08 | Changes are attributed and visible | Every policy change records who made it, when and why, and tells the subject seat. `pij state` and the seat's card show its current policy. | prime | must | [ ] planned | After a change, the seat receives one notice and `pij state` shows the policy, its setter and reason. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |
| req-09 | No new cost | The check is an in-process store read at send time. It adds no launches, polls or timers. | prime | must | [ ] planned | The PR's cost row shows 0 new launch sites and no change in `pij-rs --json ping` spawn counts. | Jordan, 2026-11-04, prime chat | — | — |

<a id="open-questions"></a>

## Open questions

| id | question | default | answer | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| q-01 | Who may change a seat's policy? Locking down is only meaningful if the seat can't unlock itself. | Its parent and the community's prime, not the seat itself. | — | open |
| q-02 | Should a seat also be able to restrict who may message it (inbound), or only who it may message (outbound)? | Outbound only for now. | — | open |
| q-03 | Which prime is always reachable: the seat's community prime, or any prime on the machine? | The prime of the seat's own project; with no community, its root ancestor. | — | open |
| q-04 | Are the human operator, the Telegram bridge and pij's own system messages (watchdog, bg results) exempt? | Yes: they are not seats, so they are always delivered and always reachable. | — | open |
